styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Old City pols, stepwells and Gandhi's ashram.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Thali feasts, street snacks and chai all day.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Sultanate monuments, mosques and the city's textile past.

stays.why: Walk to the pol lanes, Jama Masjid and the Kalupur market. Lively and central, but noisy and few mid-range rooms.
Quiet, leafy and close to the Sabarmati Ashram and Law Garden. Good mix of mid-range and business hotels.
Central for restaurants, shops and CG Road. Easy pick-up point for taxis and buses to most sights.
Newer hotels and malls, good for families and longer stays. Further from the Old City, so plan on taxis.

food: Start with a Gujarati thali: unlimited rotli, dal, shaak, rice and sweets, roughly ₹250–600 a person at mid-range places.
Street snacks to try: dhokla, khaman, fafda with jalebi (a Sunday morning favourite) and dabeli.
Old City food walks near Manek Chowk are famous; the night market there turns into street food after dark.
Ahmedabad is largely vegetarian and many places are dry (no alcohol). Check before you book a dinner.
Cheap and filling: a plate of snacks or a simple thali for under ₹150 at local cafeterias. Drink bottled or filtered water.
more_time: Swap a half-day for the Adalaj Stepwell, about 18 km north of the city; go early and take a taxi or app cab.
Add a day trip to Modhera Sun Temple and Patan's Rani ki Vav stepwell if you have a full extra day.
Craft lovers can swap an afternoon for the Calico Museum of Textiles (check opening days and book ahead) or the Auto World Vintage Car Museum.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the Old City, the stepwells and a proper thali, with time for the ashram and markets.

month_notes: January: cool and dry, highs near 27°C. The best month for walking the Old City.
February: mild and dry, highs around 31°C. Great for sightseeing and day trips.
March: warming fast, highs near 35°C. Sightsee early morning and evening.
April: hot, highs around 39°C. Keep afternoons indoors and carry water.
May: the hottest month, highs near 41°C. Avoid midday sun; plan air-conditioned stops.
June: still hot at 38°C, with the first monsoon showers (about 8 rain days).
July: monsoon peak, about 23 rain days and highs near 32°C. Carry an umbrella.
August: wet and humid, about 19 rain days. Streets can flood briefly; plan flexible days.
September: rain easing, about 14 rain days, highs near 32°C. Still humid.
October: drying out, highs near 34°C. Comfortable evenings return.
November: dry and pleasant, highs around 32°C. A strong month to visit.
December: cool and dry, highs near 28°C. Good for sightseeing; bring a light layer for evenings.

climate_guide.summary: Hot and mostly dry, with a short, heavy monsoon from June to September. November to February is the comfortable window.

items.title: Best time: November to February
items.text: Highs of 27–32°C and cool nights. Ideal for walking the Old City and day trips.

items.title: Very hot April to June
items.text: Highs of 38–41°C. Do outdoor sights at sunrise or after dark and rest indoors at midday.

items.title: Monsoon July to September
items.text: Up to 23 rain days in July. Short heavy downpours; keep plans flexible and carry an umbrella.

items.title: Humid in the rains
items.text: Sticky from June to September. Light, quick-dry clothes help.

items.title: Big day-to-night swing in winter
items.text: January lows near 14°C. A light jacket is useful in the evening.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light cotton clothes, a hat and sunscreen; an umbrella for monsoon months; a light layer for winter nights.

transit.best: Auto rickshaw or Ola/Uber for most trips; walk the Old City on foot.

modes.text: No metro yet. Don't plan around rail inside the city.

AMTS city buses and BRTS (Janmarg) buses run roughly 6AM–11PM. AMTS fares about ₹3–25; a ₹45 day pass exists but is rarely worth it. BRTS bus 1000 links the airport and Karnavati Club, max fare ₹50, every 30 min.
Ola and Uber work, plus local taxi apps. Auto rickshaws are cheap; agree the fare first or use the prepaid booth at the airport.
Possible, but driving is hectic. Most visitors do better with autos and app cabs.
Best way to explore the Old City lanes. Use cycle rickshaws for short hops.
